               <ns0:p>AND the apostles <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">The rest of the Believers, who had not only one God to their Father, but one Church to their Mother, and were born of the same Spirit, and were fed by the same Milk of the Word of God.</ns0:note>, and brethren that were in Judea, heard that the <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">This was a most incredible thing unto them who were of the Seed of <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> according to the Flesh, and were not acquainted with that Mystery that <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> should have a Seed of his Faith, upon whom all the Promises were entailed. These looked upon the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> as most execrable persons, such as the Apostle describes <ns0:hi>Ephes.</ns0:hi> 2.12. that had no hope, and were with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />out God, and therefore no less than a Miracle, and that well attested, as this was, could make them change their Opinion.</ns0:note> Gentiles also had received the word of God.</ns0:p>

               <ns0:p n="3">3 <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">This is the Objection they make against <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> That contrary to the Tradition of their Elders, and <ns0:hi>Precept of their Wise Men,</ns0:hi> he had familiarly conversed with the <ns0:hi>Gen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tiles.</ns0:hi> See <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 10 28. this they look upon as Piacular, although no conversation in order to the gaining of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> unto God, was ever forbidden; but only such as might withdraw the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> from God.</ns0:note> Saying, Thou wentest in to men uncir<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cumcised, and didst eat with them.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 But Peter <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">This great Apostle condescends to the least and weak<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />est amongst them, and gives an Account of what he had done, and the Reasons that moved him unto it, if by any means he might gain some, and confirm others.</ns0:note> rehearsed <ns0:hi>the matter</ns0:hi> from the beginning, and expounded <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> by order unto them, saying,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 10.9, &c.</ns0:note> I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision, A certain vessel descend, as it had been a great sheet, let down from heaven by four corners, and it <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">To shew that he was especially concerned in this Vision, it being for his instruction and regulation.</ns0:note> came even to me.<ns0:note place="bottom">See this whole Narration spoken to in the foregoing Chapter.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 Upon the which when I had <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">It speaking his great intention of mind upon it; God so ordering of it, that it might leave the greater impression upon him.</ns0:note> fastened mine eyes, I considered, and saw four footed beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 And I heatd a voice saying unto me, Arise, Peter, slay, and eat.<ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">He might now use them without any distinction in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />differently.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 But I said, Not so, Lord: for nothing <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">St. <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> here avoucheth, that he had lived in this cere<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />monial Righteousness, tho he thought himself far from be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing justified thereby.</ns0:note> com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mon or unclean hath at any time <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">He abstained from all the appear<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ances of that Evil.</ns0:note> entred into my mouth.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 But the voice answered me <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">This is twice spoken to St. <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> that it might be the more unquestionable with him and others: it seeming otherwise very strange; and it may be therefore twice by St. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> recorded.</ns0:note> again from hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven, What God hath cleansed, <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> call not thou common.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 And this was done <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">For the same reason but now mentioned, That God might more abundantly manifest this Mystery of the cal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ling in of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> which had been so long hid.</ns0:note> three times: and all were drawn up again <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">All this was from Heaven; unto which also it tended, namely, to bring the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> thither.</ns0:note> into heaven.</ns0:p>
